description:
Vanadium, and the metals table that settles what a speciation is worth.

#333 opened on a factor: ecoinvent's `EF v3.1` implementation gives vanadium a human-toxicity factor exactly ten times EF 3.1's own, in all fourteen rows, mantissa preserved to five significant figures, which reads as a decimal point rather than a model. **That diagnosis does not survive the measurement.** EF 3.1 ships two vanadium flows in every context, `vanadium` and `vanadium (v)`, and states 1.3532e-06 for the first and 1.3532e-05 for the second in its own workbook: the ten is EF's speciation factor for vanadium(V), which is exactly why the mantissa survives it. ecoinvent was reading the right EF row; this project was comparing it against the wrong one, because its `Vanadium V` flows were routed to the element. The issue's own body raised this as a caveat and it was the answer. The two rulings that published EF's elemental number over ecoinvent's are withdrawn with this change, and no bug report is owed.

Measuring it turned up two more things, and both are matching defects rather than factor ones. ecoinvent's thirteen `Vanadium V` flows (CAS 22537-31-1) reached *two* substances, split by nothing but the compartment -- elemental `Vanadium` from air and soil, `Vanadium(3+)` from water -- and neither is pentavalent vanadium. And the reason the right target was unreachable is that EF 3.1 gives its own thirteen `vanadium (v)` flows the registry number 15121-26-3, which belongs to vanadium(2+); the list followed the number, renamed the object `Vanadium(2+)`, and published EF's pentavalent vanadium as the divalent ion.

The rest of the file is JRC 130796 Table 6, transcribed. It is the document that says when an element carries a speciation's factor and when it carries its own -- footnote **c** for the eighteen pairs where 'the CF of the element was set equal to the CF of the speciation', and footnote **d** for antimony, arsenic and iron, where the element's is the average of two forms and belongs to neither. Both halves are claimed here, because an expectation that checked only the speciation would pass on a build that had quietly stopped publishing the element, which is half of what this issue found. Values are written as the table prints them and compared to the significant figures they state.

expectations.title: The substance EF 3.1 calls `vanadium (v)` is published with pentavalent vanadium's registry number
expectations.comment: EF 3.1 ships thirteen flows named `vanadium (v)`, one per context, and gives every one of them 15121-26-3 -- vanadium(2+)'s number. Enrichment followed the number to ChEBI 33004 and `consensus_match` renamed the object `Vanadium(2+)`, so up to `fa1f4aa` the whole of EF's pentavalent vanadium was published as the divalent ion and 22537-31-1 named no substance in the list at all. `ef-3.1-manual-fixes.json` corrects the number; the name was never in doubt, because EF spells this family with the roman numeral everywhere -- `chromium (iii)` and `chromium (vi)`, `arsenic (iii)` and `arsenic (v)`, `iron (ii)` and `iron (iii)`.

expectations.title: Every ecoinvent row carrying 22537-31-1 reaches one substance, whatever compartment it is in
expectations.comment: ecoinvent ships thirteen `Vanadium V` flows, all carrying 22537-31-1. In the 2026-08-18 build of `fa1f4aa` they reached two substances, split by nothing but the compartment: the four air and four soil rows landed on elemental `Vanadium` (7440-62-2) and the five water rows on `Vanadium(3+)` (22541-77-1). Neither is the substance the row states. This is the same defect as #46, #316 and the `Trifloxystrobin` case in #206, reached from the metals side.

expectations.title: The ecoinvent rows carrying 22537-31-1 reach the substance carrying 22537-31-1
expectations.comment: The positive half, and the reason the claim above is not satisfied by sending all thirteen rows to the element. EF 3.1 has the right target and the correspondence table does not use it: `vanadium (v)`, in all thirteen contexts. The thirteen rewrites in `ecoinvent-match-overrides.json` each keep the target *context* the table chose and change only the substance.

expectations.title: Elemental vanadium is still published, and separately
expectations.comment: The negative control for the two claims above. EF 3.1 publishes `vanadium` and `vanadium (v)` as different flows in the same thirteen contexts, with their own rows and their own factors, and moving ecoinvent's rows off the element must not merge the two or leave the element behind. Table 6 is why they carry the same ecotoxicity number and are still not the same substance: the CF of the element was *set equal to* the speciation's, which is a statement about two things agreeing rather than about one thing.

expectations.title: EF 3.1 gives elemental vanadium a human-toxicity factor of 1.3532E-06 in air
expectations.comment:
The element's own number, and half of the pair the issue compared. **#49 opened on this number and its diagnosis does not survive the measurement.** The issue reported that ecoinvent's `EF v3.1` implementation gives vanadium a human-toxicity factor exactly ten times EF 3.1's own, in all fourteen rows, with the mantissa preserved to five significant figures, and reasoned that a decimal point moving while the digits stay is a unit slip rather than a model. The digits were real. The conclusion was not: EF 3.1 ships *two* vanadium flows in every context, `vanadium` (7440-62-2) and `vanadium (v)` (pentavalent), and its own workbook states 1.3532e-06 for the first and 1.3532e-05 for the second in air/unspecified.
